correctness.rationale: In the split traceless 2×2 matrix model, b(x,y)=tr(xy). Substituting N(x)=b(v,x)u and expanding matrix commutators gives T_N(x,y)=tr(v²)tr(u[x,y])u with the stated torsion sign as an integral polynomial identity. This specializes in particular to characteristic 3. Nondegeneracy of b and surjectivity of the bracket span both descend from the split model in characteristic ≠2; the identity descends by injective scalar extension. Thus for u≠0 the torsion is identically zero exactly when b(v,v)=0. The rank-one Segre map with the covector factor identified through b takes the conic product onto the locus, and equality of reduced closed subschemes follows from the torsion equations in the split field and descent. The conic is smooth even when it has no rational point. For v=rE+sH+tF the equation is s²+rt=0, giving q²−1 admissible nonzero v. Each tensor has q−1 presentations and trace b(v,u); a given nonzero v admits q²−1 nonzero u of trace zero and q² for any fixed trace t≠0. This gives the exact overall and trace-stratum counts and N²=(tr N)N. No higher-rank classification is required.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks one extension field; the all-field and nonsplit assertions rest on the polynomial identity and descent.
The claim is only about reduced projective rank-one geometry, not an unreduced torsion scheme.

originality.rationale: Indexed record b54c91a5334b gives the exact split rank-one torsion components, not only the zero condition, and states the smooth conic and the square-zero stratum. Record 4c68434b0025 gives the rank-one idempotent count, which equals every nonzero trace stratum after rescaling. The arbitrary-form version is not stated in those sources, but follows directly by descending the exact tensor identity, and the projective product is the rank-one Segre image of the same conic. There is no genuinely distinct valuable residue. This is equivalent indexed coverage and direct implication, not a priority claim.
